questions.question: Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
questions.headline: Among the 2,047 items that say why the person started, the most common reasons are long term wealth (43%) and specific goal (25%). Among the 1,484 that say what they expected, steady long term growth (74%) leads, followed by high or quick returns (14%) and safe like fd (8%).

stats.label: Stated reason for starting (n=2047 items that say why)
What they expect (n=1484 items that say)
Who influenced them (n=2703 items that say)

questions.question: What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting?
questions.headline: Among 1,075 items that describe a change after starting, paused or stopped (25%), stayed consistent (24%) and switched fund or platform (23%) lead. Items showing a drop-off signal make up 4% of 0-3 month posts, 4% of 3-12 month posts and 6% of 12+ month posts, but few posts state the stage, so treat this as a pattern to test.

stats.label: How behaviour changes after starting (n=1075 items that say)
What happens to the SIP, 0-3 months in (n=450)
What happens to the SIP, 3-12 months in (n=179)
What happens to the SIP, 12+ months in (n=1024)

questions.question: What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?
questions.headline: Among 218 drop-off signals that give a reason: understanding & expectation (33%), SIP broke (payment / mandate / app) (26%), money or life event (24%), pulled elsewhere (17%). Falling returns matter, but they are one reason among several.

stats.label: Stated reason among drop-off signals (n=218 that state one; 319 drop-offs in total)

questions.question: What separates investors who continue from those who quietly drop off?
questions.headline: Visible drop-offs show more confusion, anxiety or frustration than people who continue (63% vs 34%). Among those who state an expectation, 78% of continuing investors expect steady long-term growth, against 78% of drop-offs. People who lapse silently never appear in public text, so this contrast cannot show what separates them.

stats.label: People continuing (n=3392): where they go when unsure
Visible drop-offs (n=319): where they go when unsure
People continuing: what they check
Visible drop-offs: what they check

Drop-offs: feelings (n=319)

questions.question: How do these patterns differ across user segments (income stability, age, source of money, who influenced them)?
questions.headline: Differences are small and rest on few items. Share showing a drop-off signal: irregular income 6.8% (n=73), variable pay 6.8% (n=117), fixed salary 3.0% (n=693). Only about 14% of items state income at all.

questions.question: What unmet needs emerge consistently across conversations?
questions.headline: Across 7,374 relevant items the biggest unmet needs are trusted human help (38%), plain language explanation (12%), reassurance whats normal (3%). Among first-year items: trusted human help (55%), plain language explanation (13%), reassurance whats normal (7%). Among drop-off signals: trusted human help (25%), flexible pause or reduce (21%), plain language explanation (18%).

stats.label: All relevant items (n=7374)
First-year items (n=751)
Drop-off signals (n=319)
